candidate.initialCode: Exact nvr24/C05 source pins before explicitly authorized internal diagnostics

firstCausalBranch.predicate: pending.TryGetValue(key,out v); v.Length <=3 after assigning values[v]=COMMITTED
firstCausalBranch.selectedValue: The exact current pending buffer for the opaque control key, not all historical prefixes.

causalAnalysis.observed: Five independent first-failure snapshots, selected current buffer lengths 2,2,1,1,1. Exact opaque Page/context/control identities retained privately; context number 6 and per-world control number 1 in each independent session. This is context ID, not proof of document incarnation count.
staticChain: Input always Add(value), then overwrites pending[key] with each current nonempty received value or removes pending for empty. KnownSensitive remains monotonic.
Commit retrieves only pending[key], assigns that value COMMITTED, and denies when length <=3. It does not promote every historical value.
Input(commit=true), Retire(prefix), and Checkpoint() all call the same Commit with no terminal-provenance discriminator.
Change/blur, submit/pagehide, disconnected-control scan, fixed checkpoint scan, and world retirement can cause Commit.
Retire promotes the last received pending state for the retiring world, without a separate proof that this buffer is terminal; it cannot read a world already destroyed.
The passed humanEditing argument is not consulted by registry selection/promotion.

Exceptions in capture/context callbacks can mark the registry unavailable; subsequent RememberSensitive/Require surfaces the same generic error in EndTakeover. First-failure state now prevents these wrappers from hiding the initial short-commit reason.
whatNotProven: Which of the Commit callers selected the short value in these five failures.
Whether a late/duplicate/intermediate editing event, genuine terminal short current value or another ordering/lifecycle transition is the deep cause.
No assertion that the historical C04 42->1 sequence is the causal event sequence of the five current failures.
No proof of ack timeout or multiple-world selection as cause; these branches did not win the first-failure capture.

minimalRepairProposedNotImplemented.focus: Terminal-state promotion/current ownership, not the short-credential protection threshold or redaction policy.
minimalRepairProposedNotImplemented.proposal: Make promotion depend on a host-owned terminal snapshot tied to exact control/document generation and event ordering. Do not treat an arbitrary last-received editing pending buffer as terminal merely because a world retires/checkpoint runs. If terminal continuity cannot be established, preserve fail-closed. Keep every observed buffer known and committed short values denied.
guardrails: Do not select the longest historical buffer as a heuristic terminal value.
Do not ignore short committed credentials.
Do not discard prefixes/old buffers or relax bounds/expiry.
Do not add sleep/retry to mask lifecycle ordering.
Do not reconstruct/rebind to a different control/world.

regressionRisks: True committed short credential could accidentally resume if terminal classification is relaxed.
Intermediate/historical sensitive material could be forgotten or leaked across navigation if ownership reconciliation is incorrect.
Legitimate backspace/replacement could be mishandled by a longest/latest heuristic.
Wrong page/world/control binding could make terminal confirmation falsely succeed.
Changing checkpoint await/lifecycle could mask STARTED/UNKNOWN or create availability regressions.
testsNeededUnderFutureAuthorization: Deterministic current-buffer/terminal-promotion tests for editing progression, backspace/replacement/clear and short true terminal credentials.
Retire/pagehide/checkpoint ordering and exact document/control-generation ownership, including late or duplicate receipts.
All three historical focal scenarios with unchanged fixtures/driver/assertions.
Short transient exact-leaf versus committed-short denial and schema-aware control-plane preservation.
Existing 24 policy tests and complete Block05 regression only after separate human authorization.
